glosses: A physical injury caused by heat, cold, electricity, radiation or caustic chemicals.

examples.text: She had second-degree burns from falling in the bonfire.
He burnt his hand in the fire.

glosses: A sensation resembling such an injury.

examples.text: chili burn from eating hot peppers

glosses: The act of burning something with fire.

examples.text: They’re doing a controlled burn of the fields.
One typical Grecian kiln engorged one thousand muleloads of juniper wood in a single burn.

glosses: An intense non-physical sting, as left by shame or an effective insult.
An effective insult, often in the expression sick burn (excellent or badass insult).
Physical sensation in the muscles following strenuous exercise, caused by build-up of lactic acid.

examples.text: One and, two and, keep moving; feel the burn!

glosses: Tobacco.

examples.text: TOM: I’m serious bruv. Put my burn and lighter and all that in my jeans please and give them here, then press the cell bell.

glosses: The writing of data to a permanent storage medium like a compact disc or a ROM chip.

examples.text: Allow additional burns enables you to create a multisession CD, which can be used again to write more data.

glosses: The operation or result of burning or baking, as in brickmaking.

examples.text: They have a good burn.

glosses: A disease in vegetables; brand.
The firing of a spacecraft's rockets in order to change its course.

examples.text: On 4 March 1999, the MCO performed its second course correction manoeuvre with a burn involving its four thrusters […]

glosses: To cause to be consumed by fire.

examples.text: He burned his manuscript in the fireplace.

glosses: To be consumed by fire, or in flames.

examples.text: He watched the house burn.

glosses: To overheat so as to make unusable.

examples.text: He burned the toast. The blacksmith burned the steel.

glosses: To become overheated to the point of being unusable.

examples.text: The grill was too hot and the steak burned.

glosses: To make or produce by the application of fire or burning heat.

examples.text: to burn a hole;  to burn letters into a block
I posted myself near a place where they had been burning charcoal, and very soon the hare came running past, close to where I was standing.

glosses: To injure (a person or animal) with heat or chemicals that produce similar damage.

examples.text: She burned the child with an iron, and was jailed for ten years.

glosses: To cauterize.
To sunburn.

examples.text: She forgot to put on sunscreen and burned.

glosses: To consume, damage, or change the condition of, as if by action of fire or heat; to affect as fire or heat does.

examples.text: to burn the mouth with pepper

This dry sorrow burns up all my tears.

[To hate is to murder as far as your hearts are concerned.] You burn with envy and anger and are not able to obtain [the gratification, the contentment, and the happiness that you seek], so you fight and war. You do not have, because you do not ask.

glosses: To be hot, e.g. due to embarrassment.

examples.text: The child’s forehead was burning with fever.  Her cheeks burned with shame.

glosses: To cause to combine with oxygen or other active agent, with evolution of heat; to consume; to oxidize.

examples.text: to burn iron in oxygen
A human being burns a certain amount of carbon at each respiration.

glosses: To combine energetically, with evolution of heat.

examples.text: Copper burns in chlorine.

glosses: To write data to a permanent storage medium like a compact disc or a ROM chip.

examples.text: We’ll burn this program onto an EEPROM one hour before the demo begins.

glosses: To render subtitles into a video's content while transcoding it, making the subtitles part of the image (hardsubs).

examples.text: My old DVD player could play DivX files but didn't recognize the subtitle file, so I had to burn them in.

glosses: To betray.

examples.text: The informant burned him.

glosses: To insult or defeat.

examples.text: I just burned you again.

glosses: To waste (time); to waste money or other resources.

examples.text: We have an hour to burn.

glosses: In certain games, to approach near to a concealed object which is sought.

examples.text: You’re cold… warm… hot… you’re burning!

glosses: To accidentally touch a moving stone.
In pontoon, to swap a pair of cards for another pair, or to deal a dead card.
To make an area of an image darker (when processing photographs in a darkroom, this is accomplished by increasing the exposure of that area to light).
To be converted to another element in a nuclear fusion reaction, especially in a star.
To discard.
To shoot someone with a firearm.
To compromise (an agent's cover story).

examples.text: He had already burned his cover with Mrs. Phillips, and it was not a mistake he intended to make again.
